answer: Recursive zero-knowledge reputation commitments bind each agent to sequentially accumulated work, while verifiable delay primitives enforce a minimum elapsed time per identity epoch; an adversary cannot haven to clone histories or wander between pseudonyms without recomputing the entire chain. Under the random oracle model, forgery reduces to inverting delayed proofs, yielding negligible success probability, so cloned identities and raven Sybils remain information-theoretically infeasible.
